replies.body:
Wake up. These models are becoming sharper and sharper

https://preview.redd.it/j2em97p9qvfh1.png?width=1416&format=png&auto=webp&s=865af09fefa7d38beb7eda47517e308dfd98f18d

Here is the picture I attached to the prompt as well as 2 pictures of rapper Babychiefdoit I took off google. Only thing I added after the first prompt was an "exit" sign in the house but it's just aesthetics and the game would have been fine without it.

replies.author: mtg_liebestod
replies.body:
Okay, I take back my point. Yes, you can provide a generic prompt and get a well-fleshed output, but whether that output will be a good/functional game will be a completely different matter. Like is this output really what you envisaged? Does it look like Animal Crossing to you? Only paper mario influence I see is the cutout characters but I imagine you wanted something more than this.

So you can't just say "here are my API keys, build a better version of Hollow Knight and list it on Steam for $20 and funnel millions of dollars into my checking account" and actually have that work, at least not yet.

replies.author: Acid_God_
replies.body:
You're adding more points to your initial critique which was focused on the complexity of the prompt. It's dishonest rethoric. Yes, I was in awe when Opus 5 generated that game as it looked better than what I was thinking of. Opus 5 can generate trash if the prompt isn't precise enough so when it doesn't you're happy and you share it on reddit.  
  
I never played animal crossing, I only gave that reference because it's the only 3D game i know with a quite minimalist childish visual signature. I never played paper mario either, the screenshot I provided above was from someone who vibe coded a game inspired from paper-mario for the character mechanics so i stole that idea. That's the only thing I wanted and opus did exactly that.

Of course it's the demo of a demo of a prototype, I'm not pretending opus 5 generated a AAA game. I'm not claiming you can become the next Ubisoft alone in your basement, I'm just showcasing what the model can do so people can be as excited about the future as I am. Cheers

replies.author: mtg_liebestod
replies.body: My point is just to say that if you want to **reliably** generate this particular game you will need more than one prompt.
